findings.title: getCalendarCredentials stores un-awaited promises and other callers are not updated
findings.body: getCalendar is now async, so `calendar` in getCalendarCredentials is a Promise. Only getConnectedCalendars was updated to await it. The returned type has changed from Calendar|null to Promise<Calendar|null>. Any other consumer that reads `.calendar` directly, such as availability or other routers, will call methods on a Promise or treat it as always truthy. Those callers should be audited, or the function should resolve the promises itself.

findings.title: Dynamic imports are created eagerly, so nothing is lazy
findings.body: Every entry is `import(...)` evaluated at module load. Importing appStore therefore kicks off loading all ~29 app packages immediately, which defeats the purpose of lazy loading. Also, a single failing import produces an unhandled rejection at startup, and rejects every later await of that key. Use functions such as `() => import(...)` to make the loading lazy.

findings.title: async forEach makes the try/catch ineffective and the deletions fire-and-forget
findings.body: The callback is now async, so `forEach` neither awaits it nor propagates its rejections. The surrounding try/catch can never catch errors from getCalendar, deleteEvent or deleteMeeting. Failures become unhandled promise rejections. The emails are sent without waiting for the deletions to complete. The same pattern is duplicated in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and in trpc bookings.tsx. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` instead.

findings.title: async forEach pushes to apiDeletes after it has been awaited
findings.body: The recurring-event branch uses `forEach(async ...)`, which is not awaited. `apiDeletes.push` happens after the awaited getCalendar and deleteEvent calls. Because deleteEvent is awaited inside the callback, the pushed values are already-resolved results, not pending promises. `Promise.all(apiDeletes)` runs before the pushes, so calendar deletions for recurring bookings are not waited on. Errors become unhandled rejections, and the response can return before the deletions finish. This pattern was made more broken by the PR's added await. Replace it with a for...of loop.
